chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Sadeer Al-Sayrafi, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who had wealth, so he took it and buried it in a place. When a year passed over it, he went to take it out from its place, so he dug the place in which he thought the wealth was buried, but did not find it. So he remained like that for three years. Then he dug the place from all its sides, and he came across the wealth with his own eyes. How should he purify it (pay Zakat)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should purify it for one year, because it was absent from him, even if he had withheld it.'
ai.seo_question: How is Zakat calculated on wealth that was buried and lost for several years before being rediscovered?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that Zakat on buried wealth is due for only one year upon recovery, as the period of concealment is treated as a time of absence (*gha'ib*) rather than active possession. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that Zakat liability is tied to the actual period of wealth availability and circulation, distinguishing it from the continuous accumulation seen in trade goods. It underscores the fairness in Islamic jurisprudence by exempting the owner from back-payments for the years the wealth was effectively out of reach.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding a man who used to have wealth for him, so he went and buried it in a place (for safekeeping). So when a year passed by over it, he went to take it out from its place. So he dug the place in which he thought that the wealth was buried in, but could not attain it. So it remained like that for three years. Then he dug the places by all its sides, and he came across the wealth exactly. How should he purify it (pay Zakāt)?’ Heasws said: ‘He should purify it (pay Zakāt) for one year, except it was absent (hidden) from him, and even if he had withheld it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Sadir al-Sayrafiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who buries a certain amount of his wealth in a certain place and after one year goes to find out. He searches and digs around in the area but fails to find it. He then after three years goes to search again and finds the amount of wealth that was lost. He (the Imam) said, ‘He pays only one year’s Zakat because it was absent from him even though he had placed it in hold.’”
